Audora turns your book or story into an audiobook where every character has their own voice.

The best adaptation of a book is the one in your head. You can see the characters in front of you and hear them talking to each other. We want an audiobook to do those characters justice: a voice that fits each of them, so a conversation actually sounds like a conversation.

Paste a story link or upload a file. Audora works out who’s speaking and gives each character a distinct voice alongside the narrator. You can start listening while the rest of the book is still being made.

companies.name: herdr
companies.one_liner: building the open agent runtime
companies.long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.

companies.name: Sentient OS
companies.one_liner: On-device AI that knows your entire life and does your work overnight.
companies.long_description:
Truly personal AI requires running inference on your life, every day. In the cloud, that’s expensive and a privacy nightmare. On your own chip, it’s free and private.

Our custom inference stack, built on a LiteRT-LM fork, runs on Macs with just 8 GB of RAM. Every night, Sentient’s on-device models process your emails, messages, Granola transcripts, files, and more, building a rich personal knowledge base on your Mac.

Your projects, conversations, commitments, and preferences. Context you’d never have the time to type into a chatbot.

That understanding powers three ways to get work done:

Sidekick: click your Mac’s notch and say “finish this for me.” It already has your context and gets to work across your apps and browser with its own cursor, while you keep working.

Proactive intelligence: wake up to work already prepared. The reply you forgot, drafted. The subscription renewing tomorrow, caught. The report you promised, ready for review. Sentient waits for your approval before acting.

Double Tap: two taps, two seconds, and the reply you would have written appears, drafted from your personal context and writing style. Just review and send.

Open source and built with privacy at its core. Over 30 enterprises use Sentient already.

Our alpha reached 4,000+ users in its first week with $0 marketing. Our launch was the top post of the month on r/macapps.

We’ve raised over $1 million with participation from Y Combinator (F26), Afore, Pioneer Fund, and a16z speedrun’s scout fund.

companies.long_description:
ChemPilot accelerates the discovery and development of next generation defense materials using AI and data from our automated wet lab. Developing a new material today takes 10+ years of trial and error. We compress that to months by screening for what can actually be made, then closing the loop: every lab result feeds back into the models so the next round is faster and smarter.

Sam, Ofir and Maor spent two years researching these materials at the Technion lab of our CSO, Prof. Alon Grinberg Dana (former MIT postdoc), working directly with defense primes and government R&D agencies. Together we bring chemical engineering, computational chemistry and AI, plus the production systems to put them to work. ChemPilot spun out of that research.

The West’s defense and dual-use industrial base runs on materials with fragile, sole-source and often adversarial supply chains. Demand for new capability is surging, and materials still take decades to develop. We’re building a new kind of chemical prime: one that can discover, develop and ultimately manufacture the materials the West needs, securely, fast and at cost.

companies.name: Veeza AI

companies.long_description: Billions of people need tourist visas to travel the world. We use AI agents to prepare applications, verify documents, secure appointments, and handle the visa process end to end.

companies.long_description: Real biology requires a wet lab, and building one takes years and a team most AI companies don't have. Petrichor runs their experiments at scale and sends back the dense, clean data their models need to learn from.

companies.name: Kailash Labs
companies.one_liner: A factory for small and specialized video reasoning models
companies.long_description:
The world generates petabytes of video every day, and almost none of it is readable to machines.  Frontier VLMs that can unlock this (like Gemini) are too expensive to run at the volume real industries have, too generic for any single task, and can't be deployed on-prem where sensitive video lives.

We are building an auto vision factory: take video plus a customer's objective, distill a frontier model, and post-train a small open model that is SOTA on that one task and serve it blazingly fast. Our first product, Marlin, is a 2B-parameter open-weights video VLM that matches Gemini-2.5-flash on dense captioning and temporal grounding at a fraction of the cost.

companies.name: Reific
companies.one_liner: RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time
companies.long_description:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. Each comes from real, de-identified records (health data, industrial sensors, compute-cluster logs), in three families: personal agents, industry, and science and compute. The world keeps moving while the agent works, so the agent must keep learning: data arrive on a clock, and every answer is checked against what actually happened. In each family, the best frontier model averages below half, and models that train on our environments improve.

We specialise in time series because almost everything that matters is recorded that way: a heartbeat, a power grid, a factory line, a GPU cluster, an experiment. No person can turn thousands of moving signals at once into the state of a system and what happens next. AI can pass the bar exam, but it still can’t watch a system for weeks and act at the right moment. It learned from what people wrote down, in environments that freeze the world and abstract it to our understanding.

Time series let us ride the exponential. The world records new data every second and time keeps grading, so each generation of models gets harder, fresher tasks. We believe humans always strive to explore. Our mission is to build the infrastructure for that exploration: the layer of the AI stack where models keep improving, out into what no one understands yet.

companies.name: Topos

companies.long_description: Topos is a neolab founded by two Harvard math dropouts, building agent swarms to bring the rigor and verifiability of mathematics to other fields. Starting in biology, we’re optimizing how agents communicate, formalize problems, and verify each other’s reasoning.

companies.name: Saccade
companies.one_liner: World's Earliest Test for Alzheimer's Biomarkers
companies.long_description:
Alzheimer's testing today is bottlenecked around the onset of symptoms, when the damage is already done. Current treatments, including the FDA-approved drugs released in 2024, don't reverse the disease; they only slow it down. Earlier detection means earlier intervention.

Eye movement changes linked to Alzheimer's surface sooner than any other biomarker, up to 15 years before symptoms appear.

We deliver a 15-minute VR assessment delivered to patients in longevity clinics:
• Tasks: patients perform visual tasks designed by neurologists to trigger a distinct oculomotor response in people with Alzheimer's or on its path
• Hardware: our patent-pending attachment connects to any VR headset on the market and captures these eye movement patterns.
• Analysis: the patterns are compared against our ML model to produce a risk analysis.

Once classified, patients can access new interventions, such as the FDA-approved drugs. They're also referred to longevity practices, neurology practices or both, depending on their stage of decline.

Testing for the earliest biomarkers allows the earliest possible intervention. In some cases, that slows the disease enough that patients outlive the onset of symptoms and never face memory loss in their lifetime.

* Keep Your Work Safe: Unlike other systems that delete everything when they finish a task, these sandboxes remember your files, code, and settings forever until you delete them.

* Pay Only for What You Use: Stop paying for idle servers. You pay a tiny fee to store your files, but you only pay for compute power during the exact minutes your AI is actively running.

* Zero Infrastructure Headaches: You don’t need to be a senior DevOps engineer or manage complex cloud networks. One simple command handles the entire backend for you.

Industrial enterprises still rely on people to coordinate disconnected software and machines, with critical knowledge held by a few experienced employees. 

Faraday builds self-improving systems that take on this operational work. We connect to existing software and machines and build training and evaluation environments around each company’s workflows and data.

As these agents take on more workflows, Faraday will be the shared runtime coordinating work between humans, agents, and robots across the business.

companies.name: Viraj Aero
companies.one_liner: Next generation gas turbines for data centers & aviation
companies.long_description:
Viraj Aero builds gas turbines that deliver both power and cooling water for data centers. It needs no grid connection and no water pipeline.

Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patented system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks.

We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions.

We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.

companies.name: Boat
companies.one_liner: The best cloud VMs for billions of agents
companies.long_description:
**Problem**

Humans used to need laptops to do their work. Now they prompt agents instead, and those agents need computers too: always-on, in large quantities, and with unlimited capabilities. 

Building and maintaining that yourself is far from trivial.

**Solution**

Boat provides powerful, simple, permissive Ubuntu VMs in the cloud. In a sandbox, an agent can work for long periods on code or on knowledge work like legal, research, reporting, and auditing.

**Why Boat and not any other cloud VM?**

1. It is ready out of the box: every sandbox ships with a desktop, chrome, languages, docker, snapshots, and templates, plus a CLI, SDK, API, and control pane for your fleet.
2. It is permissive and paradigm agnostic: any number of agents can use any number of sandboxes. Agents can run inside or use sandboxes as an external tool.
3. It is expertly crafted: we manage everything from the individual CPU to the orchestration software, which makes sandboxes stable, persistent, scalable, and secure.
4. It is the best performance and price in town: our CPUs rank first on HPC benchmarks, and sandboxes are typically 9x to 18x cheaper than other leading sandboxes.

**Further notes**

Sandboxes are hosted in Europe, which keeps prices low, and more regions are coming. Unless compliance requires it, agents don't notice the region they run in.
