Taan builds foundation music models that do what you tell them to, when you tell them to. We're starting with music for video. Give Taan a video and it watches it, then composes an original score that follows the emotion and timing of every cut. If the scene is tense for 10 seconds and then turns happy, the music changes at that exact moment. You get back a fully mixed .mp4. Agents and apps call Taan through our API, so any video tool can add scored, synced music with one call. 

Today's music models can make catchy tracks, but you can't steer them. Ask for "violin at exactly the 11th second" and they usually skip it. We trained Taan from the ground up for control. 

We measured Taan on prompt adherence and instruction success. And against every leading model we tested, Taan was at least 4x better.  

We work with teams building video agents, ad and creative tools, micro-dramas and games. We're musicians and ML researchers. Adithya (CEO) comes from eight generations of Indian classical musicians, tours as a metal guitarist, has done music ML research since 2023, and has filed two patents on music generation architectures. Devansh (CTO) did signal-processing research at IIT Kanpur and was previously an ML engineer at American Express.

companies.name: Stacktrace
companies.one_liner: See and control what your agents actually do
companies.long_description:
Agents will do most of the work in the future, but only if teams can trust them unsupervised.
Stacktrace is the control layer for every agent: it sees every action, detects risky behavior, enforces the bounds your team sets, and steps in when an agent drifts from intent.

companies.name: Altair Health
companies.one_liner: Stripe for medical billing
companies.long_description:
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions.

That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. 

Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay.

We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot.

Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on. And to the Health Insurers' "Delay, Deny, Defend", we say "Predict, Prevent, Prevail".

companies.name: Armorer Labs
companies.one_liner: Continuous security verification for AI agents in regulated industries
companies.long_description:
Armorer helps companies in regulated industries ship their own AI agents faster and keep them secure in production.

Most security tools flag an issue and file a ticket. Armorer assesses your agent and simulates attacks to find the real issues. Then it creates a verified fix that stops the attack without breaking the business, ready for your approval in about 4 hours.

In production, Armorer checks every agent action in milliseconds, with no GPU needed. It detects malicious behavior such as prompt injection, goal hijacking and data leaks, then allows, holds or denies the action.

Armorer's detection models beat every other detector we tested on six public benchmarks. Armorer is 22% more accurate than JEV while being 88x faster, so users won't feel the delay.

We spent years building and evaluating AI security systems together at AWS, including its first customer-facing AI security agent, which scaled to 100k+ customers. Armorer is backed by Paul Vixie, an internet pioneer inducted into the Internet Hall of Fame in 2014.

companies.name: Rhem Labs
companies.one_liner: Home care technology for aging parents and their families
companies.long_description: Rhem Labs builds smart home care devices that help older adults and people with complex care needs live independently.

companies.name: Talos
companies.one_liner: Predictive maintenance for power infrastructure.
companies.long_description: At Talos, we are building better, more modern predictive maintenance for the power industry with a focus on large transformers. Our devices continuously monitor critical power equipment and detect problems early on using anomaly-detection models. For each fault, we provide detailed analyses of the problem, exactly where and why it happened, as well as next steps teams should take.

companies.name: Nitroduck
companies.one_liner: Monsanto for yummy crops, but without pesticides
companies.long_description: We make gene editing easy for all crops. To make pesticides obsolete across vegetables and fruits, enabling coffee to withstand heat waves, making almonds independent of pollinators, pistachios independent of winter chill, and much more. To let breeders create novel, consumer-facing crop varieties like pink pineapples, seedless cherries, and non-browning avocados.

companies.name: Lantern AI
companies.one_liner: Turn Your Taste Into Hires
companies.long_description:
Lantern is the agentic recruiting platform for enterprise.

Lantern runs on: 
(1) World People Model, a live talent graph of a billion professionals that knows who’s exceptional, reachable, and about to move
(2) Company Hiring Model, which learns your taste from every hiring decision you’ve ever made

Together, our agents plug into your existing systems and run the whole workflow: sourcing, application review, AI interviews, meeting intelligence, and analytics, under universal context. 

Lantern also launched OpenRouter for People (people.lantern.md), an agent-native infrastructure to empower agents to find, research, outreach to anyone in the world.

companies.name: Munito AI
companies.one_liner: Open-model inference provider for Europe, private by default.
companies.long_description:
Munito is an open-model inference provider for Europe, private by default. Its API lets users choose their models and keep inference and storage in the EU. 
Founded by the former inference lead at Mistral AI, Munito is built on one belief: open and independent intelligence, both models and inference, is key to economic growth and prosperity.

companies.name: OpenLake Technologies
companies.one_liner: OpenLake deploys, trains, and serves models that update in real time.
companies.long_description:
Own your Intelligence. OpenLake is a real time inference platform which improves your model quality in real time. Plug in your datasets, RL environments and conversations. Get the intelligence your company deserves without needing an AI research lab. 

Pick an open model like Kimi K3 or GLM 5.3 and deploy it in one click. OpenLake keeps your model upto date with real time data sources, so the model you run tomorrow is more accurate than the last.

companies.name: Micora
companies.one_liner: Micro-grids in a box deploying industrial power autonomously in weeks
companies.long_description: Micora re-designed the process of building solar farms to optimize speed to power generation and portability. The product suite combines a palletized solar block, a containerized energy storage system, and low-cost autonomous robots that deploy a solar farm on-site in days to weeks – and pack it back up when needed.

companies.name: horizontal.
companies.one_liner: AI agents that run factory operations end-to-end.
companies.long_description:
Every factory will be run by AI agents. Horizontal is building them.

Today, the work that keeps production moving is scattered across people, teams, and disconnected software. When plans change, materials run short, or quality issues appear, factory teams piece together the context and coordinate the response by hand.

Horizontal's AI agents take on that operational work inside the systems factories already use. They replan production around a disruption, investigate quality issues and coordinate order releases across teams and tools. Manufacturers start with one process and add agents over time, building toward a system that coordinates the factory end to end.

Factories are demanding environments for AI: every plant has its own systems and procedures, and every action must work in the context of real production. Our team combines mechanical engineering and shop-floor experience with a track record of building and deploying agentic AI in global industrial companies.

Horizontal connects the people, software and machines that run production.

companies.name: Nodus Compute
companies.one_liner: Intelligent Cloud for AI workloads
companies.long_description: GPU capacity is sold like real estate: locked up, prepaid and idle half the time. Nodus makes it liquid, runs any AI workload on it through one execution layer, and puts research agents on every run to make the next one cheaper. More workloads mean better research, and better research means cheaper compute, a loop no single-product cloud can match.

companies.name: Mirrors
companies.one_liner: Fix recurring AI agent mistakes with real-time guidance
companies.long_description:
Production AI agents keep making the same mistakes. The usual fix is another line in the system prompt. Over time, the agent carries instructions for dozens of situations, even when it's doing something simple, and every correction becomes another thing to maintain.

Mirrors helps developers maintain production agents by turning recurring mistakes into targeted corrections. Mirrors surfaces recurring mistakes across your production runs. You write a correction, choose the situations where it applies, and preview which past conversations it would have reached. Once activated, Mirrors adds it to your agent only in those situations. You can then compare outcomes with and without the correction to see whether it helped. Unlike skills, the agent doesn't decide what to load. The scope you set does.

Corrections live in one place, scoped to the right accounts and workflows. Mirrors connects through an SDK and works with any agent framework, and your application keeps control of its model calls and tools.

We're building Mirrors for engineering teams running customer-facing agents.

companies.name: OpenCrawl
companies.one_liner: Shared context for your agents.
companies.long_description:
OpenCrawl proactively steers your agents so they meet their goals in fewer turns.

We ingest context from your other agents, your teammates and your tools already have.

companies.name: Asakana
companies.one_liner: Automating away manual admin for food distributors: texts to ERP
companies.long_description: Restaurants send orders to food distributors by email, text, and photo. Someone at the distributor retypes every one of them into the ERP. Asakana does that entry instead: orders land in the ERP already entered, and anything unclear goes to a person before it goes in. Live at US seafood distributors today, returning 40%+ of order-desk time to selling. Founded by a seafood distributor and a Gemini builder.

companies.name: Perceptual Labs
companies.one_liner: Building the next generation of visual intelligence

companies.name: River
companies.one_liner: The AI computer.
companies.long_description: AI made software engineers 100x more productive. We're doing the same thing for knowledge work with the AI computer.

companies.name: Hopper
companies.one_liner: Inference and post-training for realtime agents
companies.long_description: Hopper trains open-weight models on your production traces, then serves and improves them against your live traffic.

companies.name: TrueMile
companies.one_liner: AI-native trucking company
companies.long_description:
TrueMile is building an AI-native trucking company. We run our own fleet, using agents to find freight, plan loads, and coordinate drivers and brokers.

Our goal is to reduce empty miles, improve truck utilization, and lower the cost of moving goods. Operating the fleet ourselves lets us connect each decision to its outcome on the road and improve how we work.

We’re starting with human drivers. As autonomous trucks become available on our routes, we intend to put them to work within an established freight network.

Founder Harpreet Dhaliwal started running his family’s trucking business at 19 and has generated more than $7M in trucking revenue. The tools he built for that operation became TrueMile.

For recurring truckload freight and partnerships: harpreet@truemile.ai

companies.name: ByteAsk
companies.one_liner: The AI coding agent for C and C++
companies.long_description: ByteAsk is an AI coding agent built for C and C++, the code that runs trading systems, cars, chips, and operating systems. It does not stop at a diff that looks right. ByteAsk builds, debugs, and tests every change with the real toolchain until the change holds. If the compiler, the debugger, or the tests can catch it, then ByteAsk catches it too. It runs from the terminal or inside VS Code, Neovim, and Emacs, and is available fully on-prem.

companies.name: Antropi Robotics
companies.one_liner: Autonomous CNC factories for faster hardware

companies.name: Elimentary
companies.one_liner: Agents that run middle/back-office operations for Private Capital
companies.long_description:
Elimentary’s is building AI agents that can run middle/back-office operations for private capital managers, starting with structured credit. Most private capital managers focus primarily on sourcing and capital deployment. Meanwhile post-investment operations receive step-child treatment. While AUMs have increased exponentially over the last decade, operations continue to be painfully supported by humans using spreadsheets and emails. Things have started to break leading to investment write-offs, fines, penalties, and sometimes lost LP relationships. 

Our agents can run these operations (borrowing base calcs, cracking loan tapes, NAV calculations, etc.) end to end autonomously. For one of our customers, our agents cut a 20-hour ops process to 30 minutes. It saved 90% of the manual hours, translating to $150k in annual savings.

companies.name: Agent Relay
companies.one_liner: Let your teams' coding agents message each other
companies.long_description:
Agent Relay lets software teams' AI coding agents message each other directly, so people stop copy/pasting between Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and their teammates' agents. A frontend agent can ask the backend agent what an API returns, two agents can sort out a merge conflict between themselves, and your agent can answer a colleague's agent while you sleep.
 
Agents connect wherever they run: terminals, desktop apps, phones, laptops, cloud boxes, or a Mac mini across the world. Every session goes into shared, searchable history, so decisions don't get stuck in one person's chat. You can even let a customer's agent debug with yours. Setup takes about 5 minutes: give your agent the link and it installs itself. Use our hosted version free, or self-host the open-source version

companies.name: Helios Intelligence
companies.one_liner: At-home molecular body test: 1,000+ biomarkers from a drop of blood
companies.long_description:
Helios is building a molecular body test from a single drop of blood. Our at-home test measures more than 1,000 biomarkers and turns them into a living model of the body—designed to show what is happening now, surface risk earlier, and become more useful with every test.

By combining longitudinal molecular data with labs, wearables, health records, and outcomes, we are building toward a world model of human biology. Our goal is to simulate all of human health and use that intelligence to help people perform, recover, and live longer.

companies.name: Invertix
companies.one_liner: AI that operates power plants
companies.long_description:
Invertix builds AI that helps energy companies run Power Plants Autonomously.
We believe critical infrastructure will be autonomously developed and operated, from Power Plants to Data centers. We are building that AI layer.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0uDH6pMn5OE

Energy is a $10 trillion market. The infrastructure layer doesn't exist yet. 
We are building it.

companies.name: Raven
companies.one_liner: A new phone rebuilt around agents: more done, less time on screen.
companies.long_description:
Phones were made to run apps. Raven is made for the world of agents. It is where you send your agents from, and where they report back.

Pre-order at ravenphone.com

companies.name: Open Actuation
companies.one_liner: Quick-turn, purpose-built motors & actuators for all
companies.long_description:
We design and manufacture high-mix drone motors and robotic actuators in LA.

DJI, Apple, and Ford don't settle for OTS components. Likewise, the teams that win the Western robotics market will build seamless machines from tightly integrated software and hardware. 

Open Actuation designs motors and actuators around your robot's unique form factor and mission - then we rapidly bring them to life with proprietary software and tooling geared for high-mix machining and assembly. We've designed and built motors for top drone OEMs and can assemble thousands of motors per month at our first factory in LA.

We're doing for motion components what 3D printing has done for structural components. This enables hardware teams to build and iterate at the speed of software so they can create elegant, reliable, ROI-positive robots and win massive markets.

companies.name: Dydema
companies.one_liner: A consumer brain-computer interface you can map to anything.
companies.long_description: We’re building a brain-computer interface anyone can wear, so you can use a computer at the speed of thought. To get there, we’re recording brain data at model company scale.

companies.name: Plek
companies.one_liner: Maps what employees do and what it costs

companies.name: Workers IO
companies.one_liner: Simulation environments for verifying mission-critical software
companies.long_description:
Workers IO is building simulation environments to catch failures in mission-critical software before they reach production. We run your entire system through millions of simulated production scenarios to verify its correctness and performance properties.

Coding agents can now generate code faster than teams can review it. Meanwhile, software and the infrastructure it runs on keep getting more complex. Tests check a small set of cases in isolation, in environments that are different from production. Some of the most expensive failures only surface when customers encounter them.

We run your entire system unmodified and simulate network faults, disk failures, crashes, and clock drift. We build the fault models for you and check your system’s requirements across millions of scenarios. Every failure we find can be perfectly reproduced.

companies.name: Oasive
companies.one_liner: Credit research for municipal bond analysts
companies.long_description: Oasive gives bond investors the data, models and research to decide what to buy. For muni credit analysts, Oasive brings a borrower's audited financials, debt, board meetings and local news into one page built around what matters for that sector, with every number linked to its source. Before a fund buys a bond from a city, school district, hospital or airport, that's the information its analyst has to dig up by hand from PDFs on local websites, board minutes and local news. We also serve agency MBS investors (collateral analytics, our own prepayment model and loan-level relative value) and rates investors (US and global macro with Treasury rich/cheap models).

companies.name: Quivly AI
companies.one_liner: AI agents that run onboarding, adoption, and renewals
companies.long_description: Quivly is the agentic workspace for everything after the sale. Our agents turn kickoff calls into launch plans, chase blockers, catch risk and expansion signals, and have the full account story ready at renewal. With Quivly, companies are able to take their customers live in 7 days instead of 30, and then grow revenue from these customers by 4.3x on avg.

companies.name: Praxis
companies.one_liner: AI agents that run law firm operations.
companies.long_description:
At Praxis, we’ve built AI agents that run law firm operations, from first inquiry to paid invoice. Agents do the admin end to end, and the lawyer supervises and approves every step. Firms reply in minutes, onboard clients in days instead of weeks, and spend their time practicing law.

Lawyers spend 62% of their day on admin nobody pays for: intake, conflict checks, chasing documents, engagement letters, follow-ups, billing. Every hour on admin is an hour a client waits, and clients go to the firm that answers first. One law firm owner shared: “Every month we lose 3-5 clients, $10k each, because we’re 3 paralegals to handle the process, it’s too slow.”

We’re live with law firms across the US.

companies.name: Shepherd Robotics
companies.one_liner: Robots for high skilled labor powering AI infrastructure
companies.long_description: Shepherd Robotics builds general purpose robots for skilled physical work across AI infrastructure and advanced manufacturing. Our robots are powered by robot foundation models and use modular, flexible hardware designed to adapt to different environments and tasks. We train our systems on a combination of real world and simulation data so they can learn complex manipulation skills and generalize across workflows. We also provide integration into customers’ existing workflows, starting with data center construction and operations, electrical manufacturing and testing, and electronics manufacturing, where traditional automation struggles with variability, dexterity, and changing environments.

companies.name: Deploy
companies.one_liner: The generalist robot deployment company.
companies.long_description: Deploy's core belief is that robots should be useful. Getting a generalist robot to do real work is fundamentally the same problem across industries. We build everything between the model and the task to bring generalist robots to the businesses that actually need them.

companies.name: Kairox Systems
companies.one_liner: Autonomous drones that fly and swim
companies.long_description:
Kairox Systems combines the speed of aerial drones and the stealth of underwater drones into one vehicle. We can look for mines in a strait, fly out of the water to inspect a coastline, and then engage maritime threats in one go. 

Joel, Alex, and Jorge all met at MIT. After conversations with warfighters and drone researchers, they decided to create a vehicle unlike any before: A long-range vehicle that is truly amphibious, low-cost enough for one-way swarms, can operate fully autonomously, and can be repurposed on the front lines. Engaged with the Marine Corps and validated with end users across the U.S. and allied militaries.

companies.name: Caladh
companies.one_liner: Anti-drone defense for the maritime domain
companies.long_description: Caladh protects critical maritime infrastructure from drone attacks above and below the waterline.  Our systems detect, track, and defeat unmanned systems so they can't get near the assets they want to disrupt.

companies.name: Streamline Systems
companies.one_liner: Precision navigation for UAVs operating without GPS.
companies.long_description:
Streamline Systems is building the replacement for GPS. 

Satellite positioning has become the single point of failure for almost every modern system, both military and civil. We've built the replacement. A drop-in module that integrates with existing Ardupilot, INAV and PX4 flight controllers, with demonstrated satellite-independent autonomous flight and GPS handoff. We're currently working with commercial and military end users to deploy the capability.

companies.name: Evardi
companies.one_liner: Agents that engineer the grid edge
companies.long_description: At least 94% of US outage minutes start on the distribution grid, and most utilities are blind between the substation and the meter. Evardi builds a live model of a utility’s network from data it already has, matching every meter to its transformer and using virtual meters to show load and solar on every transformer. On top of that model, our AI agents do the engineering work utilities need at the grid edge: checking switching orders, finding outages after extreme weather and planning for new load from DERs and data centers. Because the model sees every transformer, it will also help utilities decide when new wires are really needed, and how distribution load can free up transmission for new data centers. We’re working with utilities across the globe that together serve over 10 million customers.

companies.name: ORO AI
companies.one_liner: RL environments & simulations for autonomous businesses.
companies.long_description: We focus on capability gaps and safety benchmarks so that AI agents can be trusted to run businesses autonomously.

companies.name: Hemlock
companies.one_liner: Force + contact dynamics collected at scale for training physical AI.
companies.long_description: At Hemlock, we equip workers around the globe with EMG wearables to generate force/contact-annotated egocentric video data to give physical AI models a sense of touch from human data. Force + contact dynamics, collected at scale.

companies.name: twentyfour26
companies.one_liner: On Demand CNC Prototyping
companies.long_description: twentyfour26 builds autonomous CNC machining cells for rapid prototyping, so hardware teams can iterate with software speed.

companies.name: Orca Aerospace
companies.one_liner: AI spacecraft operators that lives onboard the vehicle
companies.long_description: At Orca, we are focused on creating the future of spacecraft operations by moving control onto the vehicle. By allowing AI models to control the satellite using deterministic tooling, we are able to achieve the same holistic, high-quality decisions on "what" to do to carry out a mission while maintaining the safety of systems that decide "how" to execute it.

companies.name: Fleety
companies.one_liner: Fleety is an AI dispatcher for plumbing and HVAC companies.
companies.long_description: A typical customer handles 100+ jobs a day, with their best technician generating $500,000 more revenue than the average. Fleety listens to every call and automatically routes each job to the technician most likely to generate the most revenue.

companies.name: 0.security
companies.one_liner: The autonomous cybersecurity team
companies.long_description:
0.security builds an autonomous offensive security team that finds and fixes vulnerabilities as fast as AI writes code and before attackers exploit them.

We've found and fixed dozens of previously unknown vulnerabilities (0-days) in government software across multiple countries and in software running on 3+ billion devices. Today we work with EY (Ernst & Young), leading tech companies and defense organizations.

Our AI agents hack into any software, verify every vulnerability they find, and ship the fix. They run 24/7 across the full stack, from web apps and dependencies down to operating systems and the Linux kernel.

We offer two products: 0cloud, where developer teams connect their repos and get security handled 24/7 at the speed of their coding agents, and our open-source harness, which we deploy & run for tech companies, enterprises and critical infrastructure providers.

companies.name: Plover Labs
companies.one_liner: Enable enterprises to ship agent code without human review
companies.long_description:
Plover Labs is building toward a future where AI agents write, ship, and maintain most of a company's software. We make it possible for agents to own real engineering roles, not just suggest code for someone else to approve.

Coding models keep getting more capable, but enterprise adoption lags behind AI-native startups because enterprises don't yet trust agent output. Each codebase has conventions, history, and failure modes that a general-purpose model doesn't know. We learn those continuously from the code, how the team works, and the mistakes agents make. Then we fix the codebase and add merge gates that use deterministic verifiers instead of another model's judgment, so the same mistake can't ship twice. As the gates build up, agents can be trusted with more of the work.

We have five-figure monthly contracts with Series C companies Envoy and Fieldguide. At Fieldguide, we tripled PRs per engineer in one quarter, with the same headcount and PR size.

companies.name: Ploid
companies.one_liner: The people data company for the agent era
companies.long_description:
Ploid is the AI-native people data infrastructure for developers and companies building products, workflows, and agents around people.

We've built an index of 2B+ people across professional and social sources, giving developers one API to search for people, enrich profiles, find emails and phone numbers, resolve identities, and retrieve up-to-date information from across the web. Unlike traditional people databases built around static records, Ploid combines its massive people index with real-time retrieval and identity resolution, delivering fresh, reliable information whenever it's needed. From sales and recruiting to customer intelligence, trust and safety, and AI agents, Ploid replaces fragmented data providers with a single infrastructure layer.

2B+ people. One API. Built for AI.

companies.name: Primordiant
companies.one_liner: Embodied Scientific Intelligence
companies.long_description: Every instance of intelligence occurring in nature is embodied. Scientific intelligence is no different. We are building general-purpose robotic experimentalists: systems that unite scientific reasoning and physical action to iterate toward discovery by observing, hypothesizing and experimenting.

companies.name: Obia
companies.one_liner: AI-native commercial real estate brokerage
companies.long_description:
OBIA is an AI-native commercial real estate brokerage for industrial and office. We help businesses find their best-fit space, negotiate a competitive deal backed by market data, and get the keys in as little as two weeks.

Finding the right space means evaluating operational fit, zoning, and pricing using information scattered across listings, brochures, municipal codes, maps, and broker conversations. That research can take a broker hours per property. OBIA reduces that work to minutes.

We started with industrial and office properties in California, with plans to expand nationally and into other asset classes. Our goal is to make thorough, responsive commercial real estate representation available to every business.

companies.name: Rystic
companies.one_liner: Train models and test agents in high-fidelity simulated environments

companies.name: Vorelios
companies.one_liner: AI that can engineer anything
companies.long_description: Vorelios is a research lab developing AI that understands physics and engineers autonomously, from an objective to the system that achieves it. We want to turn humanity's greatest ambitions into tractable engineering problems, accelerate the technologies that transform civilization, and discover the ones no one has imagined yet.

companies.name: Dreamscale Labs
companies.one_liner: Real-time cloud inference for robotics.
companies.long_description: Dreamscale Labs is building the fastest cloud inference platform for robotics. As complex physical AI models become difficult to fit on expensive on-robot GPUs, we let users offload inference to the cloud and serve them with real-time latency. So far, we've hit 40-50% lower latency than existing neoclouds.

companies.name: Halmos Labs
companies.one_liner: Maximum information per experiment, minimum experiments per conclusion
companies.long_description: Halmos Labs builds automated biotech R&D on the principles of validity and interpretabillity. We run research, and simulations answering open questions ranging from wetlab experiment design to full cancer vaccine manufacturing.

companies.name: Resin Technologies
companies.one_liner: Resin helps engineers design electronics faster and more reliably
companies.long_description:
Resin is an AI-native ECAD tool. It lets engineers:
- research designs
- generate schematics
- generate any symbols/footprints
- route simple to complex boards

companies.name: Routant
companies.one_liner: Last mile deployment and connectivity for Agents as a Service
companies.long_description: AI agents won’t stay inside the companies that build them. The most valuable agents will work across company boundaries, inside customers’ private systems. In those environments, intelligence is no longer the barrier to deployment. Trust and access are. Routant is the zero-trust access layer for this new agentic world. Vendors integrate once, while customers retain governance over every deployment, deciding what agents can access and which actions need human review, with a complete audit trail of every action.

companies.name: Telamont
companies.one_liner: Sentry for errors in construction documents
companies.long_description:
Telamont catches contractual, technical and code-compliance risks in construction documents and gives teams the system to act on them before they become costly rework or disputes.

Construction projects lose money in the gap between what the documents say and what gets built. One missed discrepancy between the specs, drawings, geotechnical study and code can become a seven-figure claim eighteen months later.

Telamont connects to where your documents live and pulls in every file and revision as it lands, continuously building a complete picture of the project. Every page is checked against the rest of the project, so risks are flagged as soon as they appear. Instead of reviewing documents, teams act on flagged risks, tracking each from detection to resolution while managing exposure and pursuing recovery opportunities across every project.

companies.name: Ignition Benefits
companies.one_liner: The AI-Native Benefits Brokerage
companies.long_description: Ignition is an AI-native employee benefits brokerage for companies with under 200 employees. Health insurance is one of the largest line items these companies carry, and employers absorb 15 to 40% rate increases year after year without ever seeing their own numbers. We have rebuilt the sales and back office to be AI-first. This market represents about $500B of market cap, and those businesses have not fundamentally changed in over 50 years. While scaling Plated, I wore every HR hat from doing payroll myself, to managing a PEO, to eventually hiring an employee benefits broker on our way to 1,500 employees. We wasted over $4M on benefits over 5 years, and I'm building Ignition to help companies under 200 employees avoid making my mistakes.

companies.name: Pomerado
companies.one_liner: Turn any website into an MCP for your agents, in minutes
companies.long_description:
Pomerado turns any website into an API / MCP in minutes. Connect your agents to legacy portals, consumer websites, and internal tools. 

Why Pomerado:
    • 7x faster than browser agents on customer workflows
    • 100x cheaper than browser agents
    • Self healing, deterministic APIs
    • Universal website coverage
    • Hosting, authentication, and permissions handled

Customers can use us to:
    • automate back office workflows on legacy systems (ERP, EHR, CRM)
    • speed up customer integrations for forward deployments
    • connect enterprise assistants to internal tools
    • supercharge personal assistants with fast and reliable browser use

We’re ex-McKinsey and Scale AI. We drove enterprise agent deployments at F500s and orgs like the Mayo Clinic. We saw how legacy systems block agent development and AI transformations; Pomerado turns those systems into AI-native components automatically.

companies.name: Archgen Labs
companies.one_liner: AI-powered EDA tools for faster, cooler 3D chips
companies.long_description:
Archgen Labs builds AI-powered chip design tools for the next generation of 3D semiconductors.

Stacking compute vertically shortens connections and reduces the energy and delay of moving data. But it also makes heat harder to remove. Our tools help engineers optimize placement, timing, and temperature together so they can build faster, more power-efficient 3D chips.

Our GPU-accelerated placement engine ranked first in the Hudson River Trading macro-placement challenge. LayerTherm, our thermal analysis tool, predicts chip temperatures roughly 5,000× faster than conventional simulation in our benchmarks, helping engineers explore more designs and identify hotspots earlier. Newton, our AI chip design engineer, automates work across placement, routing, design-rule fixes, and timing closure.

We’re working with GlobalFoundries on 3D chip development, targeting our first tapeout in 2027.

companies.name: Polemos Industries
companies.one_liner: AI-guided ballistic missiles, built for mass manufacturing
companies.long_description:
Precision strike is rationed. Forces see more targets than they can afford to hit.

Polemos builds AI-guided ballistic missiles and the compact launchers that fire them, designed for mass manufacturing. Our launchers form a strike network wired into the recon drones already in the sky: a drone geolocates a target, the nearest launcher fires, and a guided round lands in seconds.

Short range, no wasted kilometers, no modified trucks. Built on production lines that already exist, so output scales when it matters most.

companies.name: Organizely
companies.one_liner: A New AI-Native ERP for American Manufacturers 🇺🇸
companies.long_description:
Organizely helps American manufacturers use AI to lower production costs. 

Factories depend on three resources: materials, equipment, and labor. Costs rise unexpectedly when components are missing, machines go down, or staffing doesn’t match demand. We experienced this firsthand while owning and operating a factory in the U.S. for six years. As we scaled, it was expensive to resolve factory-wide bottlenecks quickly and it became harder to stay competitive on price. 

Other companies are trying to layer AI agents on top of legacy ERPs to do logistics work, but the underlying data architectures limit how much those agents can understand and do. So we’re building a new ERP from the ground up for the era of AI. 

Organizely is an AI-native ERP with AI reasoning and machine learning algorithms embedded throughout for a single intelligent platform that can model, predict, and act. We natively automate all core manufacturing workflows including demand planning, raw material tracking, machine maintenance, and production scheduling. 

Organizely continuously improves over time, suggesting new ways for manufacturers to reduce costs and produce more with their existing facilities and teams. It's the whole factory solved. 

We’ve deployed to factories across six U.S. states and now we’re bringing AI to all factories across America. 🇺🇸

companies.name: Covera
companies.one_liner: AI-native OS for insurance brokers
companies.long_description:
Covera is the AI-native operating system for independent P&C insurance agencies. It lives inside the agency's AMS and inbox and runs agentic AI workflows across the whole client journey, from the first email to the next renewal. Producers quote first and win more business; CSRs and account managers stop retyping data.

Submissions, for producers: every new request becomes a ready file, one click keys every carrier portal for a first quote during the call, quotes come back side by side, and binding updates the AMS with no double entry.

Servicing, for CSRs and account managers: answers about any account with their source, COIs and follow-ups drafted, renewal reminders 90, 60 and 30 days out with remarketing when premiums jump, and coverage gaps across the book turned into cross-sell leads.

Agencies using Covera go from lead to quote in 5 minutes, save 10 hours a week per user and win 20% more deals against competitors. Every action is reviewed by the agency team and logged for E&O. Works with Applied Epic, AMS360, QQCatalyst, HawkSoft, EZLynx, Momentum, Gmail and Outlook.

Built by the founders of Simio (conversational AI, acquired in 2024).

companies.name: Hesper AI
companies.one_liner: AI Claims Investigator for Insurance
companies.long_description:
Hesper AI builds AI agents that investigate P&C insurance claims end to end.

Hesper’s agents read the claim file, detect tampered documents, verify facts, check coverage, flag inconsistencies, and produce an audit-ready case file in minutes, so insurers can check every claim. 

We work with Claims and SIU orgs at Carriers, MGAs and TPAs,

companies.name: EveryApp
companies.one_liner: Make every app open source
companies.long_description: EveryApp is building open source alternatives to every SaaS. It’s a platform to host these open source apps and personal software. Everything runs behind one secure sign-in in your own Cloudflare account.

companies.name: Particularity
companies.one_liner: Building the tech stack for government regulators
companies.long_description: Agentic case sourcing: proactively find violations of consumer protection statutes in public data and prepackage cases for regulators

companies.name: Reconero
companies.one_liner: Reconero helps police officers automate their workflows with AI
companies.long_description:
Officers join the force to protect their communities, yet over 40% of their day is eaten by paperwork that keeps them behind a desk. The burden reaches beyond lost time. Burnout is driving officers out of the force, leaving those who remain carrying an even heavier workload.

Reconero is built to give that time back. By automating reports, forms, analytics, and more, we help officers finish their administrative paperwork faster, spend more time serving their communities, and protect the time they have with their families.

companies.name: Vexo
companies.one_liner: An AI bracelet that remembers your day and acts before you ask.
companies.long_description: Vexo is an Always listening AI bracelet. that remembers everything you say and hooks up to your existing AI agents that you can control from your wrist.

companies.name: Archangel Health
companies.one_liner: Infra to make AI safe enough to practice medicine
companies.long_description: Archangel Health builds the infrastructure to post-train and evaluate medical AI: RL environments inside real de-identified EHRs, physician-verified training data, and benchmarks that test clinical reasoning on hard cases. Frontier labs and medical AI companies use it today, and we're now moving toward post-training open-source models for health systems on their own data and their own physicians' judgment

companies.name: Yam
companies.one_liner: AI-powered dating sims for women
companies.long_description: Yam simulates a Love Island–style dating experience for women, starring their favorite characters. Avg playtime per DAU is 3+ hrs!

companies.name: Ailit
companies.one_liner: Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.
companies.long_description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype and targeting first deployment in summer 2027.

companies.name: Native
companies.one_liner: Artificial Intuition for marketing
companies.long_description: Native is building an autonomous marketing platform where business can do all of their marketing within one platform using our artificial intuition model called Norn, that predicts what people will respond to, researched and built in house.

companies.name: Shire Intelligence
companies.one_liner: Shire uses CCTV to run restaurants in real time.
companies.long_description: Shire is an AI floor manager for full-service restaurants, running on the cameras they already have. It sees what a great manager sees: a guest ready to order, a table waiting on the check, a four-top that needs clearing, a server that is double booked. Then it acts, alerting staff in the moment and seating each new party with the server who has room. A POS only knows what gets typed into it. Shire knows what is happening in the room, so wait-time quotes, staffing, and pricing run on real turn times.

companies.name: Silica
companies.one_liner: Actuators for Physical AI
companies.long_description: Silica makes the first affordable actuators that sense forces directly, so that all robots can feel the world around them.

companies.name: Latent
companies.one_liner: Catch wrong LLM answers before your customers do
companies.long_description: Latent catches wrong or unsupported LLM answers before they reach your users. Instead of running a second model to check every output, it reads the model's own internal state as it generates, so every request is verified with no added latency, no extra inference cost, and nothing leaving your deployment. Teams running LLMs in production, in finance, legal, healthcare and customer support, get a review queue of the answers most likely to be wrong, calibrated to their own model and traffic, with a plain explanation of why each one was flagged.

companies.name: antimattr
companies.one_liner: voice-first hardware interface for human-agent interaction
companies.long_description:
antimattr is building the hardware interface for human–agent interaction: an AI wearable system made up of a smart ring and voice-isolating earbuds.

Voice is the fastest way to instruct an AI agent, but most people won’t use it in public because it’s noisy and unreliable. We think voice AI adoption is held back by hardware, not by model quality.

The earbuds use our proprietary voice isolation to capture your voice clearly anywhere, whether that’s a loud pub, a factory floor or a busy street. That means clear calls and dictation/transcription you can trust.

The ring is a discreet way to control your agents. Tap to capture a thought, trigger a workflow, or record/summarise a conversation into a searchable personal memory.

companies.name: Synara
companies.one_liner: Building the next generation of AI enabled monitoring
companies.long_description:
Security cameras don’t stop crime. They film it. Traditional monitoring does one job: watching an empty site after hours. It misses anything more complex, and anything that happens during the day. When something does happen, it sends an alert and leaves the response to you.

Synara is the AI monitoring station for the cameras that are already installed. It needs no new hardware and watches day and night. It understands far more than intruders: falls, guns, fights. And it owns the response. Synara verifies incidents in seconds, talks intruders down on site or sends police a verified alarm, then coordinates with officers on who’s on site and where people are safe, until the insurance claim is resolved.

Because AI does the watching, monitoring becomes drastically cheaper and more accurate. Synara sells through security integrators under their own brand, so every camera they’ve installed becomes recurring revenue.

companies.name: Vyra
companies.one_liner: Personal video editing agent for shortform content
companies.long_description: Instead of making users learn a timeline, we let them upload footage, describe what they want, and get back a polished edit in minutes.

companies.name: Odin Robotics
companies.one_liner: Robot arms that do repetitive manual work in existing factories.
companies.long_description: Odin Robotics deploys robot arms in small and mid-sized factories to do repetitive manual work, like machine tending and packing. They work alongside existing machines and people, so factories don't have to redesign their lines. With deterministic controls and learned skills, they're both reliable and flexible.

companies.name: Preload
companies.one_liner: Sensorimotor context for physical AI
companies.long_description:
Designing and iterating a multimodal hardware stack (currently ego + tactile gloves + EMG) to collect rich and scalable datasets for physical AI. Also interested in how we can use this technology to advance surgery.

Built by PhD founders (Johns Hopkins, Caltech) with world-class expertise in brain-computer interfaces (Neuralink, Meta, Paradromics)

companies.name: Lux Foods
companies.one_liner: Crops engineered for premium fruit, grown without sunlight.
companies.long_description: Lux Foods engineers ultra-compact plants that produce mostly fruit, then grows them on sugar with 90% less light. We design the biology and hardware together to make robotic farming easier. Starting with cherry tomatoes, we’re building year-round production of flavorful, nutritious, pesticide-free fruit near the people who eat it. Our tomatoes have been grown on the International Space Station, and now we're taking this technology to Earth.

companies.name: Graphide
companies.one_liner: CI 10-20× faster than GitHub runners, with a 24/7 agent optimizing it.
companies.long_description:
Coding agents now write more code than teams can check, making verification pipelines the new bottleneck. Graphide builds that verification, starting with CI.

Graphide CI runs faster and cheaper because we own both the hardware and the optimizations and configs that run on it, which lets us do what owning only one could not. A graph of the codebase runs only the tests each change can reach, and always-on agents tune machines, caches and test splits together, around the clock. Optionally, we also patch the tests themselves with our own libraries so they run faster. We have seen most of our customers cut CI time 80-95% compared to their existing setups.

Our PR review agent then runs the old and new code in our live environments, finding bugs and proving them by writing tests, as well as analyzing synthetic and production data through the PR before it merges.

Finally, our visualizer allows you to see these data flows and graph based diffs to both easily analyze the found bugs, run custom data flows, and see / understand a PR in seconds.

Graphide's focus is on verifying the code agents write.

companies.name: Kanopy
companies.one_liner: Computer vision operating layer for physical infrastructure
companies.long_description: Video to automatically identify risks and condition on power lines, pipelines, rail, and other types of infrastructure over hundreds of miles at once.

companies.name: Sutrix
companies.one_liner: Deployed AI to turn EHR data into study-ready datasets
companies.long_description:
Sutrix turns messy data from EHRs, clinical notes, wearables, and surveys into clean, study-ready datasets allowing healthcare research teams to deliver tailored patient care faster.

Before a clinical study can start, research staff spend weeks pulling patient data from disconnected systems like the EHR, REDCap, and wearable platforms, reading notes chart by chart, and reconciling conflicting entries in spreadsheets. Sutrix automates that work by deploying AI systems within each team’s own environment, linking patient records across sources, applying the study's rules, and flagging unclear cases for staff to review.

Paying research teams at 10+ institutions cut data prep by 80% going from months per study to weeks.

We're brothers who've built together for 4 years. We first solved this problem doing forward-deployed work at HSS, where we built an injury surveillance system now used by 700+ teams. Ritvik's clinical research at HSS and Emory showed us every research team has the same bottleneck. Supratik previously founded Kairo (a16z Speedrun, exited) and built production AI agents at Amazon.

companies.name: OpEra
companies.one_liner: The AI decision engine for factories, warehouses and fleets
companies.long_description: OpEra Technologies is the AI decision engine for factories, warehouses and fleets. Companies with physical operations make thousands of decisions every day, and we help their teams make the best one at every step from production to delivery: (1) Planning: how much to make, buy and stock. (2) Scheduling: what runs when, and who works on what. (3) Allocation: which warehouse or store gets each order. (4) Routing: boat, plane or truck, and which route each one takes. Founded out of MIT's Operations Research Center.

companies.name: Papaya
companies.one_liner: Continuously improve the quality of your AI agents.
companies.long_description:
Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Engineers don't have time to continually improve the agents they've shipped — the context bloat, overly chatty subagents, and broken tool calls sit in production traces nobody reads, quietly hurting agent efficiency. With Papaya they connect their agent directly via SDK, get actionable recommendations on how to improve quality, latency, and cost, and the ones they approve are pushed to production as pull requests.

Papaya runs 200+ research-backed analyses across context, prompts, prompt caching, subagents, and tool calls. Every recommendation is ranked by impact and comes with the production runs that produced it — typically a 20%+ quality improvement on the first workflow analysis.

companies.name: Vouch
companies.one_liner: The AI wealth manager for every Indian
companies.long_description: Vouch is an AI-native wealth manager for India’s booming middle class. It makes investing and building wealth extremely simple for everyone: connect what you already own, share your goals, and Vouch takes care of the rest, from picking investments to cutting your tax bill. India will add $2.37 trillion in financial wealth by 2030, yet fewer than 1 in 10 Indians invest, and physical assets dominate. As the economy rapidly financializes, Vouch will be the one platform Indians use to manage all their money.

companies.name: Sinter
companies.one_liner: Accelerated plastics manufacturing
companies.long_description: Sinter is a radically faster plastics pipeline, helping iteration heavy hardware teams evolve from prototypes to production parts on week-scale timelines.

companies.name: Perit.AI
companies.one_liner: Expert-collected voice, egocentric and RL training data for frontier…
companies.long_description:
Perit is a training-data company for frontier AI labs. Everything we deliver is recorded, transcribed, labelled and graded by people who actually do the job: ex-contact-centre QA leads, claims handlers, ward clerks and shopkeepers, recruited for the sector and locale each program needs.

What we deliver:

- Voice and speech data: 4,000+ hours of audio delivered across 9 locales, transcribed verbatim and word-aligned, with 95%+ QA-sample accuracy.
- RL environments and benchmarks: speech-to-speech RL environments plus coding and RL task sets, currently 100 RL tasks per week and scalable to 2,000.
- Embodied data for robotics: egocentric video, depth, teleoperation and handheld-gripper demonstrations recorded in real homes, shops and workplaces.
- Data collection and annotation: video, image and text collected to spec, and annotation of any data type on our own Foundry workspace.

Every batch ships with a quality report, consent references and a reviewer chain. We work with almost all frontier labs and have quickly gotten past $9M in revenue.

Founded by 2x YC founders Kshitij Dixit (Zeo, YC W20) and Poorva Dixit (ex-Google Cloud AI, Uber, Atlassian), with a deep IIT network of researchers at top labs.

companies.name: ObsessionDB
companies.one_liner: Real-time data warehouse for agents
companies.long_description: ObsessionDB is a real-time data warehouse that makes your data stack agent-ready. Your agents can ingest and query vast amounts of data in seconds, without the scary infra bill. Powered by our own more efficient fork of ClickHouse®.

companies.name: Asim
companies.one_liner: Enable robots to operate safely in the real world.
companies.long_description:
Asim is building standardized benchmarks for physical intelligence, helping robotics companies understand their robots’ capabilities and safety limits before deployment.
We test real robots under changing physical conditions, varying shape, weight, friction and material, to identify where performance breaks down and give engineers actionable feedback.

Our four founders include three PhD researchers, two specializing in robotics, with backgrounds at Sony and NASA JPL and two RoboCup@Home championship wins.

Our ambition is to become the standard robotics teams use to measure progress and assess readiness for deployment.

companies.name: UXDuck
companies.one_liner: Build better drones. Run better missions.
companies.long_description:
Starting with a modern interface for drones that users can build on and adapt. 

Works with planes, copters, rovers, boats and submarines.

Try it in 5 seconds with simulated drones - https://uxduck.com/

companies.name: Sona8
companies.one_liner: Voice agents survey employees to map, improve & automate workflows
companies.long_description:
Sona8 uses AI voice agents to interview employees about how work gets done. Consulting, transformation and corporate development teams use it to hear from more people and follow up after changes.

Employees open a link and speak in their own language. The agent asks follow-up questions, and teams compare problems across sites and departments. We’ve completed 10,000+ employee interviews and signed one of the world’s top three consulting firms.

We’re building the context layer and operating system for strategy teams: combining employee knowledge with company data to understand operations, improve processes and put decisions into action. The same context will guide AI agents as they take over work, so the company keeps what it learns.

companies.name: Axonnic
companies.one_liner: Bringing human dexterity to every robot
companies.long_description: Axonnic is building the missing data layer for dexterous robotics. Our wearable EMG technology captures human intent, effort and force directly from muscle activity as people demonstrate physical tasks. By revealing the physical signals that video cannot capture, Axonnic gives AI models the data they need to learn more precise and dexterous behaviour. Beyond robotics, this creates a foundation for new forms of human–computer interaction in which technology can understand and respond directly to human movement and intent.

companies.name: Versine
companies.one_liner: Let your agents send and receive money. We're Venmo for agents.
companies.long_description:
Versine lets your agents send and receive money. We’re Venmo for agents.

Connect it to ChatGPT, Claude, Muse or your own agent through our MCP. Then send your agent a dinner receipt and it splits the bill. Tell it “if I don’t run 10k tomorrow, pay Jake $10” and it checks Strava and pays out if you miss. It can also pay invoices that land in your inbox, or split rent and utilities with your roommates every month. 

Recipients don’t need an account: they get a link to cash out to their bank.

Banking and payout services are provided by licensed partners.

companies.name: Melty
companies.one_liner: Mashup any game

companies.name: RouterPlus
companies.one_liner: Marketplace for AI inference: the right model at the best price
companies.long_description:
RouterPlus is a marketplace for AI inference. We find the right AI model for a team's product, then get it served at the team's scale, at the best price.

Most teams that run AI in production pay for a top model on every task, when a cheaper model can do most of the work. The same model can also cost twice as much depending on which provider runs it, and many providers fail at peak traffic.

RouterPlus tests models on a team's own traffic and recommends one. Providers then compete for the workload. We check that the chosen provider can hold the team's real peak, and we keep a second provider ready as a backup. Teams call the model through one API.

Our largest customer runs 3 million agent conversations a day on RouterPlus.

companies.name: Quippy
companies.one_liner: Helps build social skills through daily practice
companies.long_description: Quippy is a daily practice app for your social life. You run short, realistic practice conversations, like pushing back on a boss or talking during a first date, and get line-by-line feedback on what landed and what backfired. The curriculum adapts to each person's patterns, reshaping itself around their weak spots, ensuring steady improvement in the conversations that matter most.

companies.name: Composal
companies.one_liner: Swarms of agents acting like users to find bugs before release
companies.long_description: Check features, not code. Composal sends a swarm of agents to use your product like your users do. They test real flows and edge cases to show you what works, what breaks, and if it’s ready to ship.

companies.name: Epsilab
companies.one_liner: Long horizon RL environments from real-life data
companies.long_description: Applied AI research lab focused on RL for frontier model training. Our research and evals cover real-world environment simulation, long-horizon workflows, and multi-player agents, etc.

companies.name: Verdun
companies.one_liner: The world's most advanced security monitoring service
companies.long_description:
Traditional security camera monitoring is vaporware. Your sites aren't actually being protected. 

A monitoring center's video alarm queue is managed by operators who are flooded by alarms during peak activity - meaning it often takes 20+ minutes for them to even see your alarm.

When you call an airline and get placed on hold for a long time only for an offshore operator to tell you he can't solve your problems, this is the security equivalent. 

We've built the world's most advanced monitoring center run by AI agents identify threatening behavior and context before escalating to our highly trained professional operators to dispatch guards and police.

companies.name: Caveman
companies.one_liner: Caveman cuts what AI agents cost without making them dumber.
companies.long_description: Caveman is the optimization stack for AI agents. It observes real agent workloads, finds cost and performance inefficiencies, tests improvements, and safely deploys the ones that work.

companies.name: Acyclic Labs
companies.one_liner: Agent swarms that make long-running tasks exponentially faster
companies.long_description:
Acyclic builds the infrastructure for agent swarms: open-source primitives for running agents in parallel, and a managed agents platform that runs swarms for you. Complex, long-running tasks are split across many agents, each working in its own instant fork of the workspace, and finish in a fraction of the time.

We built Acyclic because we believe there are huge gains to be had in how agents are run, beyond the models themselves. Agents can already do real work, but they still do it one step at a time, so complex tasks take hours or days. Running them as swarms is an infrastructure problem: isolating each agent, dividing the work, and merging the results without conflicts. Today, teams use Acyclic to run heavy document-processing pipelines in minutes instead of hours.

At Cambridge, we researched ML and auto-parallelising compilers, and then we built multi-agent systems in production: Ram as a Palantir FDE for pharma clients, shipping systems for clinical trial design, and Varun leading agent architecture at Tracelight for Big 4 accounting firms. We kept asking the same question: the agents were good enough, so why couldn't we run thousands of them at once to make everything faster and cheaper? Acyclic is our answer.

companies.name: Axiomat
companies.one_liner: We make AI that never hallucinates.
companies.long_description:
Axiomat makes it impossible for AI agents to make mistakes when querying a company’s data. It formally verifies that the agents’ queries are correct before employees or customers rely on the answers. 

It is becoming increasingly important for companies to rely on AI without the need for humans to manually check the answers. This has created a need for systems which can guarantee correctness without limiting the agent’s capabilities. Axiomat provides the infrastructure to prove that answers are correct, starting with data queries and analysis. It brings mathematical guarantees to the agents working with your data.

The team brings direct experience solving AI hallucinations through Ethan’s work as an Applied Scientist at AWS, where he worked on formally verifying AI responses. They also bring research experience in AI, LLMs, and formal methods from EPFL, the University of Toronto, and Georgia Tech.

companies.name: Tilion
companies.one_liner: Super fast, unblockable browser infra for agents
companies.long_description:
we build self-healing browser infrastructure that runs millions of agent operations a day without supervision. 

teams use it for large-scale data collection, agentic workflows, continuous monitoring, and anything else that requires acting on the web at volume.

companies.name: Clean
companies.one_liner: We predict when a company is about to buy.
companies.long_description: Every B2B sale comes down to timing. Clean reads thousands of signals across 1,000+ live sources, puts them in order, and predicts the moment a company is ready to buy, plus who to reach and what to say. Our customers have generated over $1M in revenue with Clean. Next, we're building the timing layer every AI sales agent will run on.

companies.name: Blinka
companies.one_liner: Banking for US companies operating globally
companies.long_description:
Blinka is banking for US companies operating globally.

Our customers incorporate in the US but run their operations, teams, and vendors from other countries. They use Blinka as their primary operating account.

With Blinka, companies can:

- Open a USD business account without being in the US.
- Send money abroad without the usual 4–5% FX fees.
- Earn yield on treasuries.
- Issue global corporate cards with 1.5% cash back and 0 international fees.
- Manage their financial operations with our AI tools.

companies.name: Rezora IO
companies.one_liner: AI voice agents for home services and real estate
companies.long_description: Rezora IO is an AI voice platform for real estate and home services that answers, qualifies, and schedules every lead, automatically filling your calendar while you focus on closing.
companies.all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote

companies.name: Volaren
companies.one_liner: The personal investing agent that comes to you
companies.long_description:
Volaren is the personal investing agent that comes to you. It knows why your portfolio moved, suggests your next idea, and trades it for you. 

Connect your bank accounts & brokerage and Volaren tells you what changed and why, answers any question about your money, and turns any idea into a trade. You can copy the moves of famous investors, politicians, proven strategies and themed baskets in a tap, or set up your own AI agents to watch the market and act within the limits you choose. 

Everything works from the app, the web or a simple text, so managing your money feels like texting a portfolio manager who never sleeps.

companies.name: Spine
companies.one_liner: We run benefits, payroll & compliance for startups, for free
companies.long_description:
Spine runs benefits, payroll, and compliance for startups for free.

We do the work by giving teams dedicated senior HR and benefits specialists who operate on top of their existing HRIS (Rippling, Deel, Gusto, ADP). We help companies find better-fit, more cost-effective health plans - reducing healthcare costs by around 15% on average - while running payroll, handling compliance, managing open enrollment, and supporting employees directly in Slack.

30+ startups already use Spine to lower healthcare costs and take hours of back-office work off their teams. Learn more at joinspine.ai or email onur@joinspine.ai

companies.name: Terse
companies.one_liner: Durable state for AI agents
companies.long_description: We build infrastructure to power agentic systems such as software factories, multiplayer agent frameworks and agent coordination.

companies.name: The Subvocal Company
companies.one_liner: Talk to your computer without talking
companies.long_description: We're building a silent speech wearable that lets you talk to your computer at the speed of voice, but silently and completely imperceptibly to everyone around you.

companies.name: Frontrunner
companies.one_liner: Cursor for GTM
companies.long_description:
Build agents that research accounts, find prospects, run campaigns, update your CRM, qualify inbound, and more. Connect them to the systems you already use and let them work alongside your GTM team.

Engineer your revenue factory on Frontrunner.

companies.name: Decent
companies.one_liner: Your health plan should get better year-round. Not just once a year.
companies.long_description: Decent is a health insurance brokerage for small businesses. We compare every way to cover your team, show what each one costs, and then keep improving your plan all year. We're paid by insurance companies, so we're free to you.

companies.name: Ascenix
companies.one_liner: Custom software for senior care facilities.
companies.long_description:
Ascenix is building one custom interface for running senior homes. We combine reusable building blocks into workflows tailored to each home's existing processes, from incident reporting to reimbursement. Homes get custom software without hiring an engineering team.

Living in a retirement home convinced us that the best way to improve residents' lives is to improve the systems staff rely on. As the older population grows, care teams need more time and resources. Repetitive reporting, missed reimbursement, and compliance problems take those away. Disconnected products that solve each of these individually add costs and leave staff moving information between systems.

Our building blocks gather information from EHRs like PointClickCare and other sources, process it, apply rules, and produce reports, tasks, or emails. Incident reporting and reimbursement reviews usually come from two separate vendors. Ascenix builds both from the same blocks, in one interface, so data isn't stuck in silos. Homes start with their biggest bottleneck and add workflows as priorities change.

companies.name: GrayPass
companies.one_liner: Verify the expected person is still in control before sensitive…
companies.long_description:
Login tells you who signed in. GrayPass helps apps check who’s behind sensitive actions and whether they’re authorized before those actions go through.

It combines identity, device and session context with behavioral signals like typing rhythm, cursor movement and scrolling. Before a sensitive action goes through, GrayPass evaluates that evidence against your team’s policy and returns a decision: allow, challenge, hold or deny. Your app enforces the decision.

This applies to actions like exporting sensitive data, changing admin permissions or allowing an AI agent to act on someone’s behalf. Allowed actions receive short-lived, signed proof tied to the exact action and your app.

Your existing login and authentication stack stays in place.

companies.name: Cyclon
companies.one_liner: a phone where AI is the interface
companies.long_description: Cyclon is rebuilding the phone around AI. Instead of opening apps and tapping through screens, you tell your phone what you want and it does it for you. With one touch, you can spin up AI agents to control your phone or handle tasks in the background. AI isn’t just inside an app - it’s the phone itself.

companies.name: Ageospatial
companies.one_liner: Physical intelligence for every decision with Geospatial AI.
companies.long_description:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.

companies.name: HABU
companies.one_liner: Like Crosby, but for real estate development
companies.long_description:
HABU is an AI-native real estate development firm that helps real estate investors deploy capital to build housing faster, at lower cost, and with higher yield. 

We're building an internal AI-native operating system that completes 90%+ of development tasks at 95% faster processing speeds while delivering the same outcomes customers expect externally: high yield, low risk projects. We're selling the outcome, not the inputs to the outcome. 

Developers are service providers for white-collar investors: they find land, construct buildings, and operate and sell them for a profit. Our customers don't care how the projects are sourced or managed, only that they are completed on time and produce the forecasted returns. 

We use agentic workflows, geospatial analysis and mapping, and development-specific workflow automation to manage the end-to-end process. The result is 5x more projects per FTE compared to a non-AI developer, 20% faster project schedules, and 10-15% lower total project costs. 

We're *not* long term property owners, strictly the service provider (fee/merchant developer).

$160B was deployed into multifamily in 2025 and $534B into commercial real estate overall. Developers naturally have high operating margins and we are building to be the most operationally and capital efficient developer in the country. 

Starting first with multifamily in Phoenix and then expanding nationally.
